original_question: For every polynomial automorphism of C^d, is its dynamical degree a weak Perron number whose algebraic degree is at most d - 1?
target_in_paper: §10.1, Question 38, read together with the scope set by Problem 8: the higher-dimensional polynomial-automorphism question asking whether the dynamical degree of any polynomial automorphism of C^d is a weak Perron number of degree ≤ d−1.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the substance of Question 38 very closely: it has the right objects (polynomial automorphisms of C^d), the right invariant (the dynamical degree), and the right arithmetic conclusion (weak Perron number with algebraic degree at most d−1).
missing_details: The paper asks this in the higher-dimensional regime d ≥ 3, via Problem 8 immediately above Question 38.
To be fully stand-alone, the dynamical degree should be defined as λ(f) := lim_{n→∞} (deg(f^n))^(1/n).
The existence of that limit is part of the nearby context: deg(f^(n+m)) ≤ deg(f^n) deg(f^m) for all n,m ≥ 0.
A weak Perron number is defined in the paper as an algebraic integer λ ≥ 1 such that every Galois conjugate μ satisfies |μ| ≤ λ.
The phrase 'degree ≤ d−1' refers to the algebraic degree of λ(f) over Q.
For full self-containment, deg(g) should be specified as the degree of the polynomial map g (standardly, the maximum total degree of its coordinate polynomials).

No extra hypotheses such as tameness, cubic degree, affine-triangular form, or preservation of a rational fibration belong to Question 38 itself; those appear only as motivating known cases or in neighboring questions.
refined_question: Let d ≥ 3 and let f be a polynomial automorphism of C^d. If deg(g) denotes the degree of a polynomial self-map g of C^d and λ(f) := lim_{n→∞} (deg(f^n))^(1/n) is the dynamical degree of f, must λ(f) always be a weak Perron number of algebraic degree at most d−1; that is, an algebraic integer λ ≥ 1 whose Galois conjugates μ all satisfy |μ| ≤ λ and whose degree over Q is ≤ d−1?
justification: The draft is targeting Question 38 in §10.1 essentially verbatim, not a broader neighboring problem. Problem 8 immediately above it supplies the intended scope d ≥ 3. The paragraph just before Question 38 defines the dynamical degree λ(f) from the degree-growth sequence and also defines weak Perron numbers. Section 6.1 provides the degree notation used for polynomial automorphisms. The rational-fibration clause belongs to the separate neighboring Question 39, so it should not be imported into the refined version.
